newsitem.title: USA: Energy Dept may use reactor at Hanford for tritium.
newsitem.headline: Energy Dept may use reactor at Hanford for tritium.

text.p: The Energy Department will keep the option of using an experimental reactor at its Hanford site in Washington state as a back-up source to produce tritium for nuclear weapons, a department spokeswoman said on Friday.

Critics said the move could worsen contamination at the Hanford former nuclear weapons site and detract from the cleanup there, and require moving weapons-grade plutonium long distances to Hanford to be turned into fuel for use in the reactor.

But proponents said keeping the Fast Flux Test Facility reactor on standby would be cheaper than other backup alternatives to produce tritium, the radioactive gas that starts fusions reactions in thermonuclear weapons, and also could produce cancer-treating medical isotopes.

The department stopped producing tritium in 1988 because of safety concerns with the ageing reactor that produced it and because there was a large stockpile. But it is looking for a fresh supply of the relatively short-lived gas by 2005 to maintain the nuclear arsenal.

The department planned to pursue two courses to produce tritium -- one involving buying a commercial light-water reactor, and the other to build a new accelerator facility at the department's Savannah River Site in South Carolina.
